Record, transcribe and revisit

Turn meetings, lectures, interviews and spoken ideas into notes you can revisit. Dictation Notes brings together iPhone audio recording, live speech-to-text and optional AI meeting summaries.

  • Record on iPhone, pause and resume, then transcribe with Apple speech recognition.
  • Search results take you to the matching text. Replay nearby audio when timing data is available. Gather manually marked moments and add titles or local notes.
  • Select passages, adjust the text to send, then request a summary, action items, reply draft or communication review. Open linked sources to check the result. Verify AI interpretations yourself.

Free dictation, clear data paths

Free dictation needs no API key. Apple speech recognition may process audio on the device or send it to Apple when local recognition is unavailable. Cloud transcription and AI send data directly to the provider you select and authorize. We do not run a backend receiving your recordings or transcripts.

Apple speech recognition

Recording controls

User-started iPhone and Watch audio recordings can continue in the background or with the screen locked. Stop and save to finish. Live dictation stops when you leave its screen. On Mac, start and stop from the window, menu bar or Option-Shift-D. Command-Shift-P pauses or resumes. Quitting stops capture. Obtain any required recording consent.

How a session goes

Record, review the source, then keep or share the notes you need.

Listen
Allow the microphone. On-device dictation needs no key. Add a speech provider you trust only if you want cloud transcription.
Ask
Use the four Mac shortcuts for a reply, a concept explanation, key takeaways or action items. AI requests go to the provider you configure and authorize.
Keep
History and recordings stay on the device unless you export or share them. We have nowhere to receive them.

Price, plainly

The app is free to install. The unlock is a non-consumable one-time purchase. Family Sharing is on. Restore with the same Apple ID on iPhone and Mac.

Common questions

Do I need an API key to start?

No. After you allow the microphone and speech recognition, on-device dictation works. Keys are only needed for cloud transcription and AI replies.

Is this a subscription?

iPhone · iPad (iOS 1.1.1) — One-time App Store purchase. See your storefront for the price. Basic features are free. Claim one optional 7-day Pro trial with no automatic charge when it ends. Mac retains 20 shared trial uses for cloud transcription, AI and translation, followed by a one-time unlock. AI and cloud transcription require your own API. Provider fees are separate. The app supplies no keys or credits.

Where do audio and text go?

Free dictation needs no API key. Apple speech recognition may process audio on the device or send it to Apple when local recognition is unavailable. Cloud transcription and AI send data directly to the provider you select and authorize. We do not run a backend receiving your recordings or transcripts.

Which systems and languages?

Mac 1.2.2 requires macOS 14+ and supports Apple Silicon and Intel. iPhone and iPad 1.1.1 require iOS 17+. Apple Watch requires watchOS 10+ and Pro activation on the paired iPhone. The apps offer 13 interface languages.

Do Mac and iPhone automatically sync history?

Mac, iPhone and iPad keep their own note libraries and API settings. Restoring a purchase restores access to the features. Watch recordings are transferred to the paired iPhone. Use export or sharing to move other notes between devices.

Is free dictation always offline?

No. Apple Speech prefers on-device recognition on Mac, but may send audio to Apple if an offline model is unavailable or fails. iPhone may also use Apple speech services. Offline availability depends on the language, model and system.

Record, transcribe, or summarize only where it is legal and you have any required consent. Suggested replies can be wrong and are not professional advice.
